title: The Banchet Awards announce 2027 chef and restaurant finalists in Chicago
text:
Stated Claim / Post Context:
The Banchet Awards announce 2027 chef and restaurant finalists in Chicago

New this year is the inaugural Environmental Leadership Award to chef Sarah Stegner, co-owner of Prairie Grass Cafe in Northbrook.

The 2027 Banchet Awards for Culinary Excellence have announced finalists in 12 categories plus three special recipients, including two pioneering chefs and an iconic deli in Chicago.

The local awards will also celebrate its 25th anniversary with a move to the Harris Theater at Millennium Park in the Loop. The Banchet Awards 2027 winners will be announced on Jan. 31, 2027.

“The Banchets celebrates the restaurants and the people behind them who make Chicago one of the world’s great dining cities,” said Michael Muser, executive director of The Banchet Foundation, in a release.

A secret panel chooses the finalists and winners. The panel varies, this year including food journalists, industry experts and food enthusiasts. They pay for their own dining expenses at restaurants in the city and suburbs. The Banchet Awards provides panelists with a small stipend.

The nonprofit organization’s mission is “to create a healthier, more sustainable, and more equitable food system and foster the next generation in the culinary arts through mentorship, education and job training.”

Manny’s Cafeteria & Delicatessen in the South Loop will receive the Iconic Restaurant Award, “for more than eight decades of family-owned hospitality and its enduring place in Chicago’s dining culture.”

Chef Paul Kahan will receive the Culinary Excellence Award “for his contributions to Chicago’s dining scene and mentorship of generations of hospitality professionals.”

New this year, The Banchets will present its inaugural Environmental Leadership Award to chef Sarah Stegner, co-owner of Prairie Grass Cafe in Northbrook, as well as founding member and past president of Green City Market in Lincoln Park. Stegner will be recognized “for decades of leadership supporting local farmers and advancing a healthier, more sustainable food system.”

“I am so grateful,” Stegner told the Tribune. “What I want is to have this award established as an acknowledgement for chefs who have taken a stand in leadership around lifting up our agricultural community and connecting people to the food that’s grown on our land.”

It’s different from the Michelin Green Star Award, she added, that was about the restaurants. Michelin awarded the sustainability star to Daisies in Logan Square and Feld in Ukrainian Village. The guide is phasing out the designation by the end of 2026.

Stegner mentions Greg Wade, head baker at Publican Quality Bread, who sources from father and son Marty Travis and Will Travis, seventh- and eighth-generation owners of Spence Farm in downstate Fairbury.

She also mentions César Murillo, the “Top Chef” semifinalist and former executive chef of North Pond, who works with farmer Oriana Kruszewski, best known for her Asian pears, out in the orchards and even helping at her Green City stall.

And Stegner mentions Arshiya Farheen, executive chef and owner of Verzênay bakery, who had a stall at Green City and still sources fruit from Mick Klug Farms in St. Joseph, Michigan, for house-made preserves.

“What I have tried to do with my career is be the conduit that helps people connect to local,” said Stegner.

Setting up Green City Market with founder Abby Mandel, chef Rick Bayless and the late chef Michael Altenberg was a pivotal moment not only in Stegner’s career, she added, but in the idea that they were going to commit to a lifelong project.

“And one of the things that I feel really proud of is that we have a budget of $750,000 in SNAP benefits,” said Stegner.
